en.title: Witcher 4 Leap Will Rival GTA 6's, CD Projekt Red Confirms
en.summary: CD Projekt Red has stated that the upcoming The Witcher 4 will represent a generational leap in quality, comparable to the significant advancements seen between Grand Theft Auto V and the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI. This ambitious goal aims to redefine player expectations for open-world RPGs.
en.body:
CD Projekt Red has ambitious plans for the next installment in **The Witcher** saga. The studio's joint-CEO, **Michał Nowakowski**, recently shared that they are aiming for a leap in quality between **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt** and the as-yet-unnamed **The Witcher 4** that will rival the monumental jump expected between Rockstar Games' **Grand Theft Auto V** and **Grand Theft Auto VI**. This comparison underscores CDPR's commitment to pushing the boundaries of open-world game design.


Nowakowski elaborated on this during a recent earnings call, noting that the significant time gap between titles—over a decade since **The Witcher 3**'s release—provides ample opportunity for innovation. He emphasized that **The Witcher 4** is being developed with the goal of being “significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game.” This suggests a comprehensive overhaul, touching everything from graphical fidelity to gameplay mechanics and world interactivity.

> "We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 — I think so, yes," he stated. "It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

## A New Benchmark for Open Worlds

The comparison to **GTA 5** and **GTA 6** is particularly telling. Rockstar's latest trailer for **GTA 6** showcased an unprecedented level of detail, NPC interaction, and environmental immersion, with features like extensive interior exploration and dynamic open-world activities that far surpass its predecessor. While **The Witcher** series is a fantasy RPG and not a modern-day crime simulator, the ambition to achieve a similar scale of advancement is clear. CD Projekt Red views **GTA 6** not as a direct competitor, but as an inspiration, noting that its progress has “an inspiration in many ways for our developers.” The studio insists its development process is not budget-driven, allowing them the freedom to pursue such grand visions.


## Fan Expectations and Future Possibilities

For fans of **The Witcher** franchise, this news ignites considerable excitement and anticipation. **The Witcher 3** is widely regarded as one of the greatest RPGs ever made, celebrated for its rich storytelling, compelling characters, and vast, detailed world. The prospect of a sequel built with modern technology and a similar design philosophy to the anticipated leap in **GTA 6** suggests **The Witcher 4** could set a new standard for fantasy RPGs. While specific details about gameplay mechanics, such as the depth of NPC interactions or the number of enterable locations, remain unknown, the overarching goal is to deliver a substantially more immersive and dynamic experience than ever before. The team is confident that this significant jump will resonate deeply with both long-time fans and newcomers to the Continent.

## What's Next

CD Projekt Red has confirmed that **The Witcher 4** will not be released in 2026, with a potential launch in 2027 or later being more realistic. Further details regarding the game's development and release timeline are expected to be shared in the future.

content_raw: CD Projekt Red expects a leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 that is comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6. In a recent earnings call (via Eurogamer ), CDPR was peppered with questions about GTA 6, since the developer also makes ambitious open-world games. CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski was asked whether or not the studio is looking at GTA for inspiration and if people can expect a similar leap between games. He noted that they have, indeed, observed the jump between GTA 5 and 6 before stating that fans can expect something comparable for The Witcher 4. "We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 — I think so, yes," he said. "It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4." The leap between GTA 5 and 6 is pretty absurd. There's a significant number of more things to do, particularly for those interested in roleplaying as a criminal. You can steal drugs, rob banks, knock over virtually any store on the map, and so much more. A lot of these details were either reserved for scripted missions in GTA 5 or were underbaked as open-world activities, but are fully fleshed out for you to do however you want in GTA 6. Advancements in NPCs, interactivity, immersion, and the ability to enter hundreds of interiors also make GTA 6 feel a world apart from its predecessor. Will The Witcher 4 also have tons of enterable interiors or deeper interactions with random NPCs? It's too soon to tell. It's possible that the leap for CD Projekt Red could come in a number of other ways, as The Witcher is a totally different world from GTA, after all. Maybe monster hunting will be more nuanced and involved than in The Witcher 3, similar to how GTA 6 has more engaging criminal activities. CDPR also noted that it plans to find ways to expand the game to more mainstream audiences, like GTA 6 has. GTA 6 collaborated with major mainstream artists to create original music, in addition to bold marketing campaigns that made the game difficult to ignore. The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release , and we can probably expect more looks at the game next year. CDPR also noted that it has signed a marketing agreement with PlayStation for the game, which will also cover previous games and allow for opportunities with PlayStation Plus' services.
